summary: Carefully preregistered, well‑documented paired study comparing a verifier‑assisted pipeline (deterministic validator + ≤1 automated repair) to accepting a single LLM candidate (shared_initial) across 300 paired synthetic NetOps intents using gpt-5-mini. Execution artifacts and hashes are archived. Results show baseline 299/300 unflagged passes vs. guarded 300/300; paired difference = 0.00333, exact McNemar two‑sided p = 1.0, 95% bootstrap CI [0.00,0.01]. The manuscript transparently reports design choices, limitations (single model/validator, synthetic suite, shared_initial estimand, ceiling effect), and releases full artifacts.
optional_revisions: Add a single explicit, prominent sentence in Methods stating that the preregistered pilot (n=60) was not run and that no post‑preregistration power recalculation was performed (point to the Disclosure where this appears) to ensure readers cannot miss this deviation.

In Results or Discussion, add one concise sentence clarifying that the shared_initial estimand intentionally conditions on a single LLM draw per pair and therefore excludes any verifier benefit that would arise from allowing independent alternative LLM candidates per condition (recommend a reminder of this when interpreting the null discordance).

Consider providing (or pointing more explicitly to) the exact archived low‑level repair transcript for the single rescued episode in a short machine‑readable excerpt in the artifacts index (if not already obvious) to aid reproducibility and forensic inspection; keep verbatim sensitive provider logs out of the main body as done.
